findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_guides, get_destination, get_place, get_dispatch, list_events, list_best_places, get_best_time, list_nearby, create_itinerary_link, suggest_edit, confirm_fact, get_plan, get_my_account · Private data: get_place, list_events, create_itinerary_link · Public sink: get_dispatch, create_itinerary_link, suggest_edit, get_plan, get_my_account · Destructive: delete_plan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_guides, get_destination, get_place, get_dispatch, list_events, list_best_places, get_best_time, list_nearby, create_itinerary_link, suggest_edit, confirm_fact, get_plan, get_my_account · Private data: get_place, list_events, create_itinerary_link · Public sink: get_dispatch, create_itinerary_link, suggest_edit, get_plan, get_my_account · Destructive: delete_plan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_destination" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
